headline: Independent restaurants outnumber chains here, but pothole repairs rank slowest citywide.
summary:
Ward 26 covers Humboldt Park, West Town, Logan Square, and Hermosa. A composite score of 46.83 places it 22nd out of 50, just above the citywide middle. The ward carries the lowest share of chain restaurants of the fifty and the second-lowest share of chain food stores, and its bars post some of the highest average ratings in Chicago. Aldermanic menu spending here is also the most geographically spread out of the fifty, reaching a wide range of blocks rather than clustering in one spot.

The clearest weakness is how fast the city responds once something breaks. Pothole repair time is the slowest of the fifty, over 60 days on average, and general 311 response time is second slowest, just over 16 days. Yoga and pilates studios are effectively absent, 48th of 50, and school proficiency lands at 43rd.
reading_the_rankings: Two of the weakest rankings are really the same story told twice. Pothole repair time and general 311 response time both come from the city's 311 system, and coverage gaps mean fewer than fifty wards have logged enough requests to make the comparison complete, so each ranking reflects whichever wards have enough data to sit in it, not a full match-up against every ward. Menu budget utilization tells a different kind of story. The ward spent 85.3 percent of its roughly $1.5 million annual menu allotment, which reads like solid follow-through, but that number lands only 44th, because most other wards spent an even higher share of theirs. And the ward's best ranking, the lowest chain-restaurant share in Chicago, rests on a business-license snapshot tied to a ward boundary recorded at the time it was pulled. Chicago redrew its ward lines in 2023, so a comparison against that older boundary is shaky, and whoever compiled the figure graded their own confidence in it medium, not high.

news.headline: Puerto Rican Parade And Fest Returns With Launch Of 'DIGNIDAD' Mobile Artwork
news.note: The 48th annual Puerto Rican parade returned to the Division Street corridor in Humboldt Park, with a large new mobile artwork touring on a flatbed truck.

news.headline: Humboldt Park Bathrooms Open For Summer
news.note: Four of the five public restrooms at Humboldt Park reopened for the season, including one near the basketball courts that had stayed closed for years.

news.headline: Avondale, Humboldt Park Projects OK'd By Council Include Housing And Animal Rescue Expansion
news.note: City Council approved a $12 million health and job training facility for a local nonprofit at 3446 W. North Ave. in Humboldt Park.
